blocks.html_en: Los Alamos conversation
[edit]
<figcaption id="mwcA">Enrico Fermi (Los Alamos 1945)</figcaption>

sentences.zh: 恩里科·费米（洛斯阿拉莫斯 1945 年）

blocks.html_en: Enrico Fermi was a Nobel Prize-winning physicist who predicted the existence of neutrinos and helped create the first artificial nuclear reactor, an early feat of the Manhattan Project.[14] He was known to pose simple but seemingly unanswerable questions—termed "Fermi questions"—to his colleagues and students, like "How many atoms of Caesar's last breath do you inhale with each lungful of air?"[15]

sentences.en: Enrico Fermi was a Nobel Prize-winning physicist who predicted the existence of neutrinos and helped create the first artificial nuclear reactor, an early feat of the Manhattan Project.[14] He was known to pose simple but seemingly unanswerable questions—termed "Fermi questions"—to his colleagues and students, like "How many atoms of Caesar's last breath do you inhale with each lungful of air?"[15]
sentences.zh: 恩里科·费米是一位获得诺贝尔奖的物理学家，他预测了中微子的存在，并帮助创建了第一个人造核反应堆，这是曼哈顿计划的早期壮举。 [14]众所周知，他向同事和学生提出了简单但看似无法回答的问题，称为“费米问题”，例如“你每吸一口空气，会吸入凯撒最后一口气中有多少个原子？”[15]

blocks.html_en: In 1950,[note 1] Fermi visited Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico and, while walking to the Fuller Lodge for lunch, conversed with fellow physicists Emil Konopinski, Edward Teller, and Herbert York about reports of flying saucers and the feasibility of faster-than-light travel.[18] When the conversation shifted to unrelated topics at the lodge, Fermi blurted a question variously recalled as: "Where is everybody?" (Teller), "Don't you ever wonder where everybody is?" (York), or "But where is everybody?" (Konopinski).[19] According to Teller, "The result of his question was general laughter because of the strange fact that, in spite of Fermi's question coming out of the blue, everybody around the table seemed to understand at once that he was talking about extraterrestrial life."[20]

sentences.en: In 1950,[note 1] Fermi visited Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico and, while walking to the Fuller Lodge for lunch, conversed with fellow physicists Emil Konopinski, Edward Teller, and Herbert York about reports of flying saucers and the feasibility of faster-than-light travel.[18] When the conversation shifted to unrelated topics at the lodge, Fermi blurted a question variously recalled as: "Where is everybody?"
sentences.zh: 1950年，[注1]费米参观了新墨西哥州的洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室，在步行前往富勒旅馆吃午餐时，与物理学家埃米尔·科诺平斯基、爱德华·泰勒和赫伯特·约克讨论了有关飞碟和超光速旅行的可行性的报告。 [18]当谈话转向旅馆里不相关的话题时，费米脱口而出一个问题，人们回忆起来是这样的：“大家都在哪儿？”

sentences.en: (Teller), "Don't you ever wonder where everybody is?"
sentences.zh: （出纳员），“你难道不知道每个人都在哪里吗？”
（约克），或者“但是每个人都在哪里？”

sentences.en: (Konopinski).[19] According to Teller, "The result of his question was general laughter because of the strange fact that, in spite of Fermi's question coming out of the blue, everybody around the table seemed to understand at once that he was talking about extraterrestrial life."[20]
sentences.zh: （科诺平斯基）。[19]据泰勒说，“他的问题引起了大家的笑声，因为一个奇怪的事实是，尽管费米的问题出乎意料，但桌子周围的每个人似乎都立刻明白他在谈论外星生命。”[20]

blocks.html_en: According to York, Fermi "followed up with a series of calculations on the probability of earthlike planets, the probability of life given an earth, the probability of humans given life, the likely rise and duration of high technology, and so on. He concluded on the basis of such calculations that we ought to have been visited long ago and many times over."[21] However, Teller recalled that Fermi did not elaborate on his question beyond "perhaps a statement that the distances to the next location of living beings may be very great and that, indeed, as far as our galaxy is concerned, we are living somewhere in the sticks, far removed from the metropolitan area of the galactic center."[20][note 2]

sentences.en: According to York, Fermi "followed up with a series of calculations on the probability of earthlike planets, the probability of life given an earth, the probability of humans given life, the likely rise and duration of high technology, and so on.
sentences.zh: 根据约克的说法，费米“随后对类地行星的概率、地球产生生命的概率、人类产生生命的概率、高科技的可能兴起和持续时间等进行了一系列计算。

sentences.en: He concluded on the basis of such calculations that we ought to have been visited long ago and many times over."[21] However, Teller recalled that Fermi did not elaborate on his question beyond "perhaps a statement that the distances to the next location of living beings may be very great and that, indeed, as far as our galaxy is concerned, we are living somewhere in the sticks, far removed from the metropolitan area of the galactic center."[20][note 2]
sentences.zh: 他根据这些计算得出的结论是，我们应该在很久以前就被访问过，并且多次被访问过。”[21]然而，泰勒回忆说，费米没有详细说明他的问题，除了“也许是一个声明，到生物的下一个位置的距离可能非常远，而且，事实上，就我们的银河系而言，我们生活在远离银河系中心大都市区的地方。”[20][注2]
俄罗斯火箭科学家康斯坦丁·齐奥尔科夫斯基

blocks.html_en: Fermi was not the first to note the paradox. In his 1686 book Conversations on the Plurality of Worlds, Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle—later the secretary of the French Academy of Sciences—constructs a dialogue in which Fontenelle's claims of "intelligent beings exist in other worlds, for instance the Moon" are refuted by a character who notes that "If this were the case, the Moon's inhabitants would already have come to us before now."[24] This may have inspired a similar discussion in Jules Verne's 1865 novel Around the Moon, which has also been identified as an early conceptualization of the Fermi paradox.[25]

sentences.en: Fermi was not the first to note the paradox.
sentences.zh: 费米并不是第一个注意到这个悖论的人。

sentences.en: In his 1686 book Conversations on the Plurality of Worlds, Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle—later the secretary of the French Academy of Sciences—constructs a dialogue in which Fontenelle's claims of "intelligent beings exist in other worlds, for instance the Moon" are refuted by a character who notes that "If this were the case, the Moon's inhabitants would already have come to us before now."[24] This may have inspired a similar discussion in Jules Verne's 1865 novel Around the Moon, which has also been identified as an early conceptualization of the Fermi paradox.[25]
sentences.zh: 伯纳德·勒·博维尔·德·丰特内尔（Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle）（后来担任法国科学院秘书）在其 1686 年出版的《关于多个世界的对话》一书中构建了一段对话，其中丰特内尔关于“智慧生物存在于其他世界，例如月球”的说法被一个人物反驳，该人物指出，“如果是这样的话，月球上的居民早就来到了我们这里。”[24] 这可能激发了类似的想法儒勒·凡尔纳 1865 年的小说《绕月》中的讨论，也被认为是费米悖论的早期概念化。 [25]

blocks.html_en: Another early formulation of the Fermi paradox was presented and dissected in the 1930s writings of Russian rocket scientist Konstantin Tsiolkovsky.[26] Although his rocketry work was embraced by the materialist Soviets, his philosophical writings were suppressed and unknown for most of the 20th century.[27] Tsiolkovsky noted that critics refute the existence of advanced extraterrestrial life as such civilizations would have visited humanity or left some detectable evidence.[28] He posed a solution to the paradox: humanity is quarantined by aliens to protect its independent cultural development, which resembles the zoo hypothesis proposed by John Ball.[29]

sentences.en: Another early formulation of the Fermi paradox was presented and dissected in the 1930s writings of Russian rocket scientist Konstantin Tsiolkovsky.[26] Although his rocketry work was embraced by the materialist Soviets, his philosophical writings were suppressed and unknown for most of the 20th century.[27] Tsiolkovsky noted that critics refute the existence of advanced extraterrestrial life as such civilizations would have visited humanity or left some detectable evidence.[28] He posed a solution to the paradox: humanity is quarantined by aliens to protect its independent cultural development, which resembles the zoo hypothesis proposed by John Ball.[29]
sentences.zh: 费米悖论的另一个早期表述在 1930 年代俄罗斯火箭科学家康斯坦丁·齐奥尔科夫斯基 (Konstantin Tsiolkovsky) 的著作中提出并进行了剖析。 [26]尽管他的火箭工作受到唯物主义苏联人的拥护，但他的哲学著作在 20 世纪的大部分时间里都受到压制和不为人知。 [27]齐奥尔科夫斯基指出，批评者驳斥了先进的外星生命的存在，因为此类文明会访问人类或留下一些可检测的证据。 [28]他提出了解决悖论的办法：人类被外星人隔离以保护其独立的文化发展，这类似于约翰·鲍尔提出的动物园假说。 [29]

sentences.en: Carl Sagan, seen here beside a Viking lander mockup, first mentioned the paradox in print.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·萨根（Carl Sagan）站在维京登陆器模型旁边，他首先在印刷品中提到了这个悖论。

blocks.html_en: The Fermi question first appeared in print in a footnote of a 1963 paper by Carl Sagan.[30] Two years later, Stephen Dole noted the dilemma at a symposium—"If there are so many advanced forms of life around, where is everybody?"—but did not attribute it to Fermi.[31] A chapter of Intelligent Life in the Universe, co-authored by Sagan and Iosif Shklovsky, was headlined with the Fermi-attributed "Where are they?"[31] The Fermi question also appeared in NASA's 1970 Project Cyclops report, a 1973 book by Sagan, and a 1975 article in JBIS Interstellar Studies by David Viewing that first described it as a paradox.[32][31]

sentences.en: The Fermi question first appeared in print in a footnote of a 1963 paper by Carl Sagan.[30] Two years later, Stephen Dole noted the dilemma at a symposium—"If there are so many advanced forms of life around, where is everybody?"—but did not attribute it to Fermi.[31] A chapter of Intelligent Life in the Universe, co-authored by Sagan and Iosif Shklovsky, was headlined with the Fermi-attributed "Where are they?"[31] The Fermi question also appeared in NASA's 1970 Project Cyclops report, a 1973 book by Sagan, and a 1975 article in JBIS Interstellar Studies by David Viewing that first described it as a paradox.[32][31]
sentences.zh: 费米问题首次出现在 Carl Sagan 1963 年论文的脚注中。[30]两年后，斯蒂芬·多尔在一次研讨会上注意到了这个困境——“如果周围有这么多先进的生命形式，那么每个人都在哪里？”——但没有将其归因于费米。 [31]萨根和约瑟夫·什克洛夫斯基合着的《宇宙中的智能生命》一章的标题是费米问题“它们在哪里？”[31] 费米问题也出现在 NASA 1970 年独眼巨人计划报告、萨根 1973 年出版的书以及 David Viewing 1975 年发表在 JBIS 星际研究中的文章中，该文章首次将其描述为悖论。[32][31]

blocks.html_en: Later that year, Michael Hart published a detailed examination of the paradox in the Quarterly Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society.[28] Hart, who concluded that "we are the first civilization in our Galaxy", proposed four broad categories of solutions to the paradox: those that are physical (a space travel limitation), sociological (aliens choose not to visit Earth), temporal (aliens have not had time to travel to Earth), or that extraterrestrials have already visited.[28][33] His paper sparked significant interest in the paradox among academics and even politicians, with a discussion held in the House of Lords.[34] A seminal response—"Extraterrestrial intelligent beings do not exist"—was written by Frank Tipler, who argued that, if an advanced extraterrestrial civilization existed, their self-replicating spacecraft should have already been detected in the Solar System.[35] The term "Fermi paradox" was coined in a 1977 article by David Stephenson and was widely adopted.[30]

sentences.en: Later that year, Michael Hart published a detailed examination of the paradox in the Quarterly Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society.[28] Hart, who concluded that "we are the first civilization in our Galaxy", proposed four broad categories of solutions to the paradox: those that are physical (a space travel limitation), sociological (aliens choose not to visit Earth), temporal (aliens have not had time to travel to Earth), or that extraterrestrials have already visited.[28][33] His paper sparked significant interest in the paradox among academics and even politicians, with a discussion held in the House of Lords.[34] A seminal response—"Extraterrestrial intelligent beings do not exist"—was written by Frank Tipler, who argued that, if an advanced extraterrestrial civilization existed, their self-replicating spacecraft should have already been detected in the Solar System.[35] The term "Fermi paradox" was coined in a 1977 article by David Stephenson and was widely adopted.[30]
sentences.zh: 同年晚些时候，迈克尔·哈特在《皇家天文学会季刊》上发表了对该悖论的详细研究。 [28]哈特得出的结论是“我们是银河系中的第一个文明”，他提出了四大类解决悖论的解决方案：物理的（太空旅行限制）、社会的（外星人选择不访问地球）、时间的（外星人没有时间前往地球）或外星人已经访问过。 [28][33]他的论文引起了学者甚至政治家对这一悖论的极大兴趣，并在上议院进行了讨论。 [34]弗兰克·蒂普勒 (Frank Tipler) 撰写了一篇具有开创性的回应——“外星智慧生物并不存在”，他认为，如果存在先进的外星文明，那么他们的自我复制航天器应该已经在太阳系中被发现。 [35] “费米悖论”一词是 David Stephenson 在 1977 年的一篇文章中创造的，并被广泛采用。 [30]

blocks.html_en: The popularization of the Fermi paradox damaged search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) efforts, and Senator William Proxmire cited Tipler when he spurred the termination of the federally funded NASA SETI program in 1981.[33] According to Robert Gray, the paradox may contribute to a "de facto prohibition on government support for research in a branch of astrobiology".[30]

sentences.en: The popularization of the Fermi paradox damaged search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) efforts, and Senator William Proxmire cited Tipler when he spurred the termination of the federally funded NASA SETI program in 1981.[33] According to Robert Gray, the paradox may contribute to a "de facto prohibition on government support for research in a branch of astrobiology".[30]
sentences.zh: 费米悖论的普及损害了搜寻外星智慧生物 (SETI) 的努力，参议员威廉·普罗克斯迈尔 (William Proxmire) 在 1981 年推动终止联邦政府资助的 NASA SETI 计划时引用了蒂普勒的话。 [33]罗伯特·格雷认为，这一悖论可能导致“事实上禁止政府支持天体生物学分支的研究”。 [30]

blocks.html_en: Fermi did not publish anything regarding the paradox, with Sagan once suggesting the quote to be apocryphal.[33][28][note 3] Scientists like Robert Gray have criticized its attribution to Fermi, and alternative terms like the "Hart–Tipler argument" or "Tsiolkovsky–Fermi–Viewing–Hart paradox" have been proposed.[37][38] According to Gray, the current understanding of the paradox misinterprets Fermi's question and subsequent discussion, which was challenging the feasibility of interstellar travel rather than the existence of advanced extraterrestrial life.[39]

sentences.en: Fermi did not publish anything regarding the paradox, with Sagan once suggesting the quote to be apocryphal.[33][28][note 3] Scientists like Robert Gray have criticized its attribution to Fermi, and alternative terms like the "Hart–Tipler argument" or "Tsiolkovsky–Fermi–Viewing–Hart paradox" have been proposed.[37][38] According to Gray, the current understanding of the paradox misinterprets Fermi's question and subsequent discussion, which was challenging the feasibility of interstellar travel rather than the existence of advanced extraterrestrial life.[39]
sentences.zh: 费米没有发表任何有关该悖论的内容，萨根曾认为这句话是杜撰的。[33][28][注3]像罗伯特·格雷这样的科学家批评了费米的贡献，并提出了诸如“哈特-蒂普勒论证”或“齐奥尔科夫斯基-费米-观察-哈特悖论”等替代术语。[37][38]格雷认为，目前对这一悖论的理解误解了费米的问题和随后的讨论，这挑战的是星际旅行的可行性，而不是先进的外星生命的存在。 [39]

blocks.html_en: The Fermi paradox is a conflict between the argument that scale and probability seem to favor intelligent life being common in the universe, and the total lack of evidence of intelligent life having ever arisen anywhere other than on Earth.

sentences.en: The Fermi paradox is a conflict between the argument that scale and probability seem to favor intelligent life being common in the universe, and the total lack of evidence of intelligent life having ever arisen anywhere other than on Earth.
sentences.zh: 费米悖论是规模和概率似乎有利于智慧生命在宇宙中普遍存在的论点与完全缺乏证据表明智慧生命在地球以外的任何地方出现过之间的冲突。

blocks.html_en: The first aspect of the Fermi paradox is a function of the scale or the large numbers involved: there are an estimated 200–400 billion stars in the Milky Way[40] (2–4 × 1011) and 70 sextillion (7×1022) in the observable universe.[41] Even if intelligent life occurs on only a minuscule percentage of planets around these stars, there might still be a great number of extant civilizations, and if the percentage were high enough it would produce a significant number of extant civilizations in the Milky Way. This assumes the mediocrity principle, by which Earth is a typical planet.

sentences.en: The first aspect of the Fermi paradox is a function of the scale or the large numbers involved: there are an estimated 200–400 billion stars in the Milky Way[40] (2–4 × 1011) and 70 sextillion (7×1022) in the observable universe.[41] Even if intelligent life occurs on only a minuscule percentage of planets around these stars, there might still be a great number of extant civilizations, and if the percentage were high enough it would produce a significant number of extant civilizations in the Milky Way.
sentences.zh: 费米悖论的第一个方面是所涉及的规模或数量的函数：银河系中估计有 200-4000 亿颗恒星[40] (2-4 × 1011)，可观测宇宙中有 70 亿颗恒星 (7×1022)。 [41]即使智慧生命只出现在这些恒星周围的一小部分行星上，仍然可能存在大量现存文明，如果比例足够高，银河系中将产生大量现存文明。

sentences.en: This assumes the mediocrity principle, by which Earth is a typical planet.
sentences.zh: 这是假设平庸原则，地球是一个典型的行星。

blocks.html_en: The second aspect of the Fermi paradox is the argument of probability: given intelligent life's ability to overcome scarcity, and its tendency to colonize new habitats, it seems possible that at least some civilizations would be technologically advanced, seek out new resources in space, and colonize their star system and, subsequently, surrounding star systems. Since there is no known evidence on Earth, or elsewhere in the known universe, of other intelligent life after 13.8 billion years of the universe's history, there is a conflict requiring a resolution. Some examples of possible resolutions are that intelligent life is rarer than is thought, that assumptions about the general development or behavior of intelligent species are flawed, or, more radically, that the scientific understanding of the nature of the universe is quite incomplete.

sentences.en: The second aspect of the Fermi paradox is the argument of probability: given intelligent life's ability to overcome scarcity, and its tendency to colonize new habitats, it seems possible that at least some civilizations would be technologically advanced, seek out new resources in space, and colonize their star system and, subsequently, surrounding star systems.
sentences.zh: 费米悖论的第二个方面是概率论：考虑到智慧生命克服稀缺性的能力，以及它殖民新栖息地的倾向，似乎至少有一些文明会在技术上先进，在太空中寻找新的资源，并殖民他们的恒星系统，随后殖民周围的恒星系统。

sentences.en: Since there is no known evidence on Earth, or elsewhere in the known universe, of other intelligent life after 13.8 billion years of the universe's history, there is a conflict requiring a resolution.
sentences.zh: 由于在宇宙 138 亿年的历史之后，地球上或已知宇宙的其他地方还没有其他智慧生命存在的已知证据，因此存在需要解决的冲突。

sentences.en: Some examples of possible resolutions are that intelligent life is rarer than is thought, that assumptions about the general development or behavior of intelligent species are flawed, or, more radically, that the scientific understanding of the nature of the universe is quite incomplete.
sentences.zh: 可能的解决方案的一些例子是，智慧生命比想象的要稀有，关于智慧物种的一般发展或行为的假设是有缺陷的，或者更根本的是，对宇宙本质的科学理解相当不完整。

blocks.html_en: The Fermi paradox can be asked in two ways.[note 4] The first is, "Why are no aliens or their artifacts found on Earth, or in the Solar System?". If interstellar travel is possible, even the "slow" kind nearly within the reach of Earth technology, then it would only take from 5 million to 50 million years to colonize the galaxy.[42] This is relatively brief on a geological scale, let alone a cosmological one. Since there are many stars older than the Sun, and since intelligent life might have evolved earlier elsewhere, the question then becomes why the galaxy has not been colonized already. Even if colonization is impractical or undesirable to all alien civilizations, large-scale exploration of the galaxy could be possible by probes. These might leave detectable artifacts in the Solar System, such as old probes or evidence of mining activity, but none of these have been observed.

sentences.en: The Fermi paradox can be asked in two ways.[note 4] The first is, "Why are no aliens or their artifacts found on Earth, or in the Solar System?".
sentences.zh: 费米悖论可以通过两种方式提出。[注4]第一个是“为什么在地球或太阳系中没有发现外星人或他们的文物？”。

sentences.en: If interstellar travel is possible, even the "slow" kind nearly within the reach of Earth technology, then it would only take from 5 million to 50 million years to colonize the galaxy.[42] This is relatively brief on a geological scale, let alone a cosmological one.
sentences.zh: 如果星际旅行是可能的，即使是地球技术几乎可以达到的“慢速”旅行，那么只需 500 万到 5000 万年就能殖民银河系。 [42]这在地质尺度上相对简短，更不用说在宇宙尺度上了。

sentences.en: Since there are many stars older than the Sun, and since intelligent life might have evolved earlier elsewhere, the question then becomes why the galaxy has not been colonized already.
sentences.zh: 由于有许多恒星比太阳更古老，而且智慧生命可能在其他地方更早进化，所以问题就变成了为什么银河系还没有被殖民。

sentences.en: Even if colonization is impractical or undesirable to all alien civilizations, large-scale exploration of the galaxy could be possible by probes.
sentences.zh: 即使殖民对于所有外星文明来说都是不切实际或不受欢迎的，但通过探测器对银河系进行大规模探索也是可能的。

sentences.en: These might leave detectable artifacts in the Solar System, such as old probes or evidence of mining activity, but none of these have been observed.
sentences.zh: 这些可能会在太阳系中留下可检测到的文物，例如旧探测器或采矿活动的证据，但这些都尚未被观察到。

blocks.html_en: The second form of the question is "Why are there no signs of intelligence elsewhere in the universe?". This version does not assume interstellar travel, but includes other galaxies as well. For distant galaxies, travel times may well explain the lack of alien visits to Earth, but a sufficiently advanced civilization could potentially be observable over a significant fraction of the size of the observable universe.[43] Even if such civilizations are rare, the scale argument indicates they should exist somewhere at some point during the history of the universe, and since they could be detected from far away over a considerable period of time, many more potential sites for their origin are within range of human observation. It is unknown whether the paradox is stronger for the Milky Way galaxy or for the universe as a whole.[44]

sentences.en: The second form of the question is "Why are there no signs of intelligence elsewhere in the universe?".
sentences.zh: 问题的第二种形式是“为什么宇宙其他地方没有智慧的迹象？”。

sentences.en: This version does not assume interstellar travel, but includes other galaxies as well.
sentences.zh: 这个版本不假设星际旅行，但也包括其他星系。

sentences.en: For distant galaxies, travel times may well explain the lack of alien visits to Earth, but a sufficiently advanced civilization could potentially be observable over a significant fraction of the size of the observable universe.[43] Even if such civilizations are rare, the scale argument indicates they should exist somewhere at some point during the history of the universe, and since they could be detected from far away over a considerable period of time, many more potential sites for their origin are within range of human observation.
sentences.zh: 对于遥远的星系，旅行时间可以很好地解释为什么外星人没有造访地球，但在可观测宇宙的很大一部分范围内，可能可以观测到足够先进的文明。 [43]即使这样的文明很罕见，规模论也表明它们应该存在于宇宙历史上的某个时刻的某个地方，而且由于它们可以在相当长的一段时间内从很远的地方被探测到，因此更多潜在的起源地点都在人类观察的范围之内。

sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚该悖论对于银河系还是对于整个宇宙来说是否更强。 [44]

The first scientific meeting on the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), which had 10 attendees including Frank Drake and Carl Sagan, speculated that the number of civilizations was roughly between 1,000 and 100,000,000 civilizations in the Milky Way galaxy.[47] Conversely, Frank Tipler and John D. Barrow used pessimistic numbers and speculated that the average number of civilizations in a galaxy is much less than one.[48]

blocks.html_en: Almost all arguments involving the Drake equation suffer from the overconfidence effect, a common error of probabilistic reasoning about low-probability events, by guessing specific numbers for likelihoods of events whose mechanism is not understood, such as the likelihood of abiogenesis on an Earth-like planet, with estimates varying over many hundreds of orders of magnitude. An analysis that takes into account some of the uncertainty associated with this lack of understanding has been carried out by Anders Sandberg, Eric Drexler and Toby Ord.[46] They suggest that there is "a substantial ex ante probability of there being no other intelligent life in our observable universe".

sentences.zh: 几乎所有涉及德雷克方程的论点都受到过度自信效应的影响，这是对低概率事件进行概率推理的常见错误，通过猜测机制尚不明确的事件可能性的具体数字，例如类地行星上自然发生的可能性，其估计值相差数百个数量级。

sentences.zh: Anders Sandberg、Eric Drexler 和 Toby Ord 进行了一项分析，考虑到了与缺乏理解相关的一些不确定性。[46]他们认为，“在我们可观测的宇宙中，存在着很大的事前概率不存在其他智慧生命”。

blocks.html_en: Dennis Danielson and Christopher Graney have argued that optimistic interpretations of the Drake equation are an artefact of history rather than of science. They show that, in the 17th and 18th centuries, the presumption that planets suitable for organic life are abundant became established in the absence of scientific evidence to support it, or even despite the scientific evidence then available against it. The presumption endured into the present day despite evidence for planetary and stellar diversity that has accumulated since the late 19th century. Thus, in their view, what is seen as the Fermi Paradox is simply science overcoming a historical presumption that never adequately recognized the importance of discoveries about, for example, the nature of planets or the origin of life.[49][50]

sentences.en: Dennis Danielson and Christopher Graney have argued that optimistic interpretations of the Drake equation are an artefact of history rather than of science.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯·丹尼尔森和克里斯托弗·格雷尼认为，对德雷克方程的乐观解释是历史的产物，而不是科学的产物。

sentences.en: They show that, in the 17th and 18th centuries, the presumption that planets suitable for organic life are abundant became established in the absence of scientific evidence to support it, or even despite the scientific evidence then available against it.
sentences.zh: 他们表明，在 17 世纪和 18 世纪，在缺乏科学证据支持的情况下，甚至尽管当时有科学证据反对这一假设，“适合有机生命存在的行星丰富”这一假设仍然成立。

sentences.en: The presumption endured into the present day despite evidence for planetary and stellar diversity that has accumulated since the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 尽管自 19 世纪末以来已经积累了行星和恒星多样性的证据，但这一假设一直持续到今天。

sentences.en: Thus, in their view, what is seen as the Fermi Paradox is simply science overcoming a historical presumption that never adequately recognized the importance of discoveries about, for example, the nature of planets or the origin of life.[49][50]
sentences.zh: 因此，在他们看来，费米悖论只不过是科学克服了历史假设，而历史假设从未充分认识到行星本质或生命起源等发现的重要性。 [49][50]

blocks.html_en: The Great Filter, a concept introduced by Robin Hanson in 1996, represents whatever natural phenomena that would make it unlikely for life to evolve from inanimate matter to an advanced civilization.[51][3] The most commonly agreed-upon low probability event is abiogenesis: a gradual process of increasing complexity of the first self-replicating molecules by a randomly occurring chemical process. Other proposed great filters are the emergence of eukaryotic cells[note 5] or of meiosis or some of the steps involved in the evolution of a brain-like organ capable of complex logical deductions.[52]

sentences.en: The Great Filter, a concept introduced by Robin Hanson in 1996, represents whatever natural phenomena that would make it unlikely for life to evolve from inanimate matter to an advanced civilization.[51][3] The most commonly agreed-upon low probability event is abiogenesis: a gradual process of increasing complexity of the first self-replicating molecules by a randomly occurring chemical process.
sentences.zh: 大过滤器是罗宾·汉森 (Robin Hanson) 于 1996 年提出的一个概念，它代表了任何使生命不可能从无生命物质进化为先进文明的自然现象。[51][3]最普遍认可的低概率事件是自然发生：通过随机发生的化学过程，第一个自我复制分子的复杂性逐渐增加的过程。

sentences.en: Other proposed great filters are the emergence of eukaryotic cells[note 5] or of meiosis or some of the steps involved in the evolution of a brain-like organ capable of complex logical deductions.[52]
sentences.zh: 其他提出的伟大过滤器是真核细胞的出现[注5]或减数分裂或能够进行复杂逻辑推论的类脑器官进化中涉及的一些步骤。 [52]

blocks.html_en: Astrobiologists Dirk Schulze-Makuch and William Bains, reviewing the history of life on Earth, including convergent evolution, concluded that transitions such as oxygenic photosynthesis, the eukaryotic cell, multicellularity, and tool-using intelligence are likely to occur on any Earth-like planet given enough time. They argue that the Great Filter may be abiogenesis, the rise of technological human-level intelligence, or an inability to settle other worlds because of self-destruction or a lack of resources.[53] Paleobiologist Olev Vinn has suggested that the great filter may have universal biological roots related to evolutionary animal behavior.[54]

sentences.en: Astrobiologists Dirk Schulze-Makuch and William Bains, reviewing the history of life on Earth, including convergent evolution, concluded that transitions such as oxygenic photosynthesis, the eukaryotic cell, multicellularity, and tool-using intelligence are likely to occur on any Earth-like planet given enough time.
sentences.zh: 天体生物学家德克·舒尔茨-马库赫和威廉·贝恩斯回顾了地球生命的历史，包括趋同进化，得出的结论是，只要有足够的时间，任何类地行星上都可能发生含氧光合作用、真核细胞、多细胞生物和使用工具的智能等转变。

sentences.en: They argue that the Great Filter may be abiogenesis, the rise of technological human-level intelligence, or an inability to settle other worlds because of self-destruction or a lack of resources.[53] Paleobiologist Olev Vinn has suggested that the great filter may have universal biological roots related to evolutionary animal behavior.[54]
sentences.zh: 他们认为，大过滤可能是自然发生、人类水平智能技术的兴起，或者由于自我毁灭或缺乏资源而无法定居其他世界。 [53]古生物学家 Olev Vinn 认为，这个伟大的过滤器可能具有与动物进化行为相关的普遍生物学根源。 [54]

blocks.html_en: In 2021, the concepts of quiet, loud, and grabby aliens were introduced by Hanson et al. The proposed "loud" aliens expand rapidly in a highly detectable way throughout the universe and endure, while "quiet" aliens are hard or impossible to detect and eventually disappear. "Grabby" aliens prevent the emergence of other civilizations in their sphere of influence, which expands at a rate near the speed of light. The authors argue that if loud civilizations are rare, as they appear to be, then quiet civilizations are also rare. The paper suggests that humanity's existing stage of technological development is relatively early in the potential timeline of intelligent life in the universe, as loud aliens would otherwise be observable by astronomers.[55][56]

sentences.en: In 2021, the concepts of quiet, loud, and grabby aliens were introduced by Hanson et al. The proposed "loud" aliens expand rapidly in a highly detectable way throughout the universe and endure, while "quiet" aliens are hard or impossible to detect and eventually disappear.
sentences.zh: 2021 年，Hanson 等人提出了安静、大声和贪婪的外星人的概念。拟议中的“大声”外星人以高度可检测的方式在整个宇宙中迅速扩张并持续存在，而“安静”外星人则很难或不可能被检测到并最终消失。

sentences.en: "Grabby" aliens prevent the emergence of other civilizations in their sphere of influence, which expands at a rate near the speed of light.
sentences.zh: “贪婪”外星人阻止其他文明在其势力范围内出现，其势力范围以接近光速的速度扩张。

sentences.en: The authors argue that if loud civilizations are rare, as they appear to be, then quiet civilizations are also rare.
sentences.zh: 作者认为，如果像表面上那样喧闹的文明很罕见，那么安静的文明也很罕见。

sentences.en: The paper suggests that humanity's existing stage of technological development is relatively early in the potential timeline of intelligent life in the universe, as loud aliens would otherwise be observable by astronomers.[55][56]
sentences.zh: 该论文表明，人类现有的技术发展阶段在宇宙中智能生命的潜在时间轴中相对较早，否则天文学家就可以观测到大声的外星人。 [55][56]

blocks.html_en: Earlier in 2013, Anders Sandberg and Stuart Armstrong examined the potential for intelligent life to spread intergalactically throughout the universe and the implications for the Fermi Paradox. Their study suggests that with sufficient energy, intelligent civilizations could potentially colonize the entire Milky Way galaxy within a few million years, and spread to nearby galaxies in a timespan that is cosmologically brief. They conclude that intergalactic colonization appears possible with the resources of a single planetary system and that intergalactic colonization is of comparable difficulty to interstellar colonization, and therefore the Fermi paradox is much sharper than commonly thought.[57]

sentences.en: Earlier in 2013, Anders Sandberg and Stuart Armstrong examined the potential for intelligent life to spread intergalactically throughout the universe and the implications for the Fermi Paradox.
sentences.zh: 2013 年初，安德斯·桑德伯格 (Anders Sandberg) 和斯图尔特·阿姆斯特朗 (Stuart Armstrong) 研究了智慧生命在整个宇宙中跨星系传播的潜力以及对费米悖论的影响。

sentences.en: Their study suggests that with sufficient energy, intelligent civilizations could potentially colonize the entire Milky Way galaxy within a few million years, and spread to nearby galaxies in a timespan that is cosmologically brief.
sentences.zh: 他们的研究表明，只要有足够的能量，智慧文明就有可能在几百万年内殖民整个银河系，并在宇宙学上短暂的时间跨度内传播到附近的星系。

sentences.en: They conclude that intergalactic colonization appears possible with the resources of a single planetary system and that intergalactic colonization is of comparable difficulty to interstellar colonization, and therefore the Fermi paradox is much sharper than commonly thought.[57]
sentences.zh: 他们的结论是，利用单一行星系统的资源，星际殖民似乎是可能的，而且星际殖民的难度与星际殖民相当，因此费米悖论比通常认为的要尖锐得多。 [57]

blocks.html_en: Critics such as David Kipping have contended that the "Grabby Aliens" model is reliant on unproven assumptions, lacking enough scientific rigor to be empirically falsifiable, and suggested other explanations for the proposed earliness of humans such as planets in M-dwarf systems being uninhabitable. Robin Hanson has responded to these criticisms.[58]

sentences.en: Critics such as David Kipping have contended that the "Grabby Aliens" model is reliant on unproven assumptions, lacking enough scientific rigor to be empirically falsifiable, and suggested other explanations for the proposed earliness of humans such as planets in M-dwarf systems being uninhabitable.
sentences.zh: 大卫·基平等批评家认为，“Grabby Aliens”模型依赖于未经证实的假设，缺乏足够的科学严谨性，无法凭经验证伪，并提出了对人类早期存在的其他解释，例如 M-矮星系统中的行星不适合居住。

sentences.en: Robin Hanson has responded to these criticisms.[58]
sentences.zh: 罗宾·汉森对这些批评做出了回应。[58]

blocks.html_en: Anthropic reasoning and the question of why we happen to find ourselves as humans creates a number of potential problems for astrobiology. Walter Barta argues that Hanson's grabby aliens model creates an anthropic dilemma. According to Hanson's model, most observers in our reference class should be grabby aliens themselves. This leads to the question of why we do not find ourselves as grabby aliens, but rather as a species confined to a single planet.[59]

sentences.en: Anthropic reasoning and the question of why we happen to find ourselves as humans creates a number of potential problems for astrobiology.
sentences.zh: 人择推理以及为什么我们碰巧发现自己是人类的问题给天体生物学带来了许多潜在的问题。

sentences.en: Walter Barta argues that Hanson's grabby aliens model creates an anthropic dilemma.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·巴塔认为，汉森贪婪的外星人模型造成了人择困境。

sentences.en: According to Hanson's model, most observers in our reference class should be grabby aliens themselves.
sentences.zh: 根据汉森的模型，我们参考类中的大多数观察者本身应该是贪婪的外星人。

sentences.en: This leads to the question of why we do not find ourselves as grabby aliens, but rather as a species confined to a single planet.[59]
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：为什么我们没有发现自己是贪婪的外星人，而是被限制在一个星球上的物种。 [59]

blocks.html_en: There are two parts of the Fermi paradox that rely on empirical evidence—that there are many potentially habitable planets, and that humans see no evidence of life. The first point, that many suitable planets exist, was an assumption in Fermi's time, but is since supported by the discovery that exoplanets are common. Existing models predict billions of habitable worlds in the Milky Way.[60]

sentences.en: There are two parts of the Fermi paradox that rely on empirical evidence—that there are many potentially habitable planets, and that humans see no evidence of life.
sentences.zh: 费米悖论有两个部分依赖于经验证据——​​存在许多潜在的宜居行星，以及人类没有看到生命的证据。

sentences.en: The first point, that many suitable planets exist, was an assumption in Fermi's time, but is since supported by the discovery that exoplanets are common.
sentences.zh: 第一点，即存在许多合适的行星，是费米时代的一个假设，但此后得到了系外行星很常见的发现的支持。

sentences.en: Existing models predict billions of habitable worlds in the Milky Way.[60]
sentences.zh: 现有模型预测银河系中有数十亿个宜居世界。[60]

blocks.html_en: The second part of the paradox, that humans see no evidence of extraterrestrial life, is also an active field of scientific research. This includes both efforts to find any indication of life,[61] and efforts specifically directed to finding intelligent life. These searches have been made since 1960, and several are ongoing.[note 6]

sentences.en: The second part of the paradox, that humans see no evidence of extraterrestrial life, is also an active field of scientific research.
sentences.zh: 悖论的第二部分，即人类没有看到外星生命的证据，也是科学研究的一个活跃领域。

sentences.en: This includes both efforts to find any indication of life,[61] and efforts specifically directed to finding intelligent life.
sentences.zh: 这包括寻找任何生命迹象的努力，[61] 以及专门针对寻找智慧生命的努力。

sentences.en: These searches have been made since 1960, and several are ongoing.[note 6]
sentences.zh: 这些搜寻自 1960 年以来一直在进行，其中一些正在进行中。[注 6]

blocks.html_en: Although astronomers do not usually search for extraterrestrials, they have observed phenomena that they could not immediately explain without positing an intelligent civilization as the source. For example, pulsars, when first discovered in 1967, were called little green men (LGM) because of the precise repetition of their pulses.[62] In all cases, explanations with no need for intelligent life have been found for such observations,[note 7] but the possibility of discovery remains.[63] Proposed examples include asteroid mining that would change the appearance of debris disks around stars,[64] or spectral lines from nuclear waste disposal in stars.[65]

sentences.en: Although astronomers do not usually search for extraterrestrials, they have observed phenomena that they could not immediately explain without positing an intelligent civilization as the source.
sentences.zh: 尽管天文学家通常不寻找外星人，但他们观察到了一些现象，如果不将智慧文明作为源头，他们就无法立即解释这些现象。

sentences.en: For example, pulsars, when first discovered in 1967, were called little green men (LGM) because of the precise repetition of their pulses.[62] In all cases, explanations with no need for intelligent life have been found for such observations,[note 7] but the possibility of discovery remains.[63] Proposed examples include asteroid mining that would change the appearance of debris disks around stars,[64] or spectral lines from nuclear waste disposal in stars.[65]
sentences.zh: 例如，脉冲星在 1967 年首次发现时，因其脉冲的精确重复而被称为小绿人 (LGM)。 [62]在所有情况下，此类观察都已找到不需要智慧生命的解释，[注7]，但发现的可能性仍然存在。[63]提议的例子包括小行星采矿，这将改变恒星周围碎片盘的外观，[64]或恒星核废料处理的谱线。[65]

blocks.html_en: Electromagnetic emissions
[edit]

sentences.en: Radio telescopes are often used by SETI projects.
sentences.zh: SETI 项目经常使用射电望远镜。

blocks.html_en: Radio technology and the ability to construct a radio telescope are presumed to be a natural advance for technological species,[66] theoretically creating effects that might be detected over interstellar distances. The careful searching for non-natural radio emissions from space may lead to the detection of alien civilizations. Sensitive alien observers of the Solar System, for example, would note unusually intense radio waves for a G2 star due to Earth's television and telecommunication broadcasts. In the absence of an apparent natural cause, alien observers might infer the existence of a terrestrial civilization. Such signals could be either "accidental" by-products of a civilization, or deliberate attempts to communicate, such as the Arecibo message. It is unclear whether "leakage", as opposed to a deliberate beacon, could be detected by an extraterrestrial civilization. The most sensitive radio telescopes on Earth, as of 2019, would not be able to detect non-directional radio signals (such as broadband) even at a fraction of a light-year away,[67] but other civilizations could hypothetically have much better equipment.[68][69]

sentences.en: Radio technology and the ability to construct a radio telescope are presumed to be a natural advance for technological species,[66] theoretically creating effects that might be detected over interstellar distances.
sentences.zh: 无线电技术和建造射电望远镜的能力被认为是技术物种的自然进步，[66]理论上产生的效应可以在星际距离上被检测到。

sentences.en: The careful searching for non-natural radio emissions from space may lead to the detection of alien civilizations.
sentences.zh: 仔细寻找来自太空的非自然无线电发射可能会导致发现外星文明。

sentences.en: Sensitive alien observers of the Solar System, for example, would note unusually intense radio waves for a G2 star due to Earth's television and telecommunication broadcasts.

sentences.en: In the absence of an apparent natural cause, alien observers might infer the existence of a terrestrial civilization.
sentences.zh: 在没有明显的自然原因的情况下，外星观察者可能会推断出地球文明的存在。

sentences.en: Such signals could be either "accidental" by-products of a civilization, or deliberate attempts to communicate, such as the Arecibo message.

sentences.en: It is unclear whether "leakage", as opposed to a deliberate beacon, could be detected by an extraterrestrial civilization.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚“泄漏”（而不是故意的信标）是否可以被外星文明检测到。

sentences.en: The most sensitive radio telescopes on Earth, as of 2019, would not be able to detect non-directional radio signals (such as broadband) even at a fraction of a light-year away,[67] but other civilizations could hypothetically have much better equipment.[68][69]
sentences.zh: 截至 2019 年，地球上最灵敏的射电望远镜即使在一光年之外也无法探测到非定向无线电信号（例如宽带），[67] 但其他文明假设可能拥有更好的设备。 [68][69]

blocks.html_en: A number of astronomers and observatories have attempted and are attempting to detect such evidence, mostly through SETI organizations such as the SETI Institute and Breakthrough Listen. Several decades of SETI analysis have not revealed any unusually bright or meaningfully repetitive radio emissions.[70]

blocks.html_en: Conjectures about interstellar probes

sentences.zh: 关于星际探测器的猜想

blocks.html_en: [edit]

The Hart–Tipler conjecture is a form of contraposition which states that because no interstellar probes have been detected, there likely is no other intelligent life in the universe, as such life should be expected to eventually create and launch such probes.[79][80] Self-replicating probes could exhaustively explore a galaxy the size of the Milky Way in as little as a million years.[12] If even a single civilization in the Milky Way attempted this, such probes could spread throughout the entire galaxy. Another speculation for contact with an alien probe—one that would be trying to find human beings—is an alien Bracewell probe. Such a hypothetical device would be an autonomous space probe whose purpose is to seek out and communicate with alien civilizations (as opposed to von Neumann probes, which are usually described as purely exploratory). These were proposed as an alternative to carrying a slow speed-of-light dialogue between vastly distant neighbors. Rather than contending with the long delays a radio dialogue would suffer, a probe housing an artificial intelligence would seek out an alien civilization to carry on a close-range communication with the discovered civilization. The findings of such a probe would still have to be transmitted to the home civilization at light speed, but an information-gathering dialogue could be conducted in real time.[81]

blocks.html_en: Direct exploration of the Solar System has yielded no evidence indicating a visit by aliens or their probes. Detailed exploration of areas of the Solar System where resources would be plentiful may yet produce evidence of alien exploration,[82][83] though the entirety of the Solar System is relatively vast and difficult to investigate. Attempts to signal, attract, or activate hypothetical Bracewell probes in Earth's vicinity have not succeeded.[84]

blocks.html_en: Searches for stellar-scale artifacts
[edit]

sentences.en: A variant of the speculative Dyson sphere.
sentences.zh: 投机戴森球的一种变体。

sentences.en: Such large-scale artifacts would drastically alter the spectrum of a star.
sentences.zh: 如此大规模的人工制品会极大地改变恒星的光谱。

blocks.html_en: In 1959, Freeman Dyson observed that every developing human civilization constantly increases its energy consumption, and he conjectured that a civilization might try to harness a large part of the energy produced by a star. He proposed a hypothetical "Dyson sphere" as a means: a shell or cloud of objects enclosing a star to absorb and utilize as much radiant energy as possible. Such a feat of astroengineering would drastically alter the observed spectrum of the star involved, changing it at least partly from the normal emission lines of a natural stellar atmosphere to those of black-body radiation, probably with a peak in the infrared. Dyson speculated that advanced alien civilizations might be detected by examining the spectra of stars and searching for such an altered spectrum.[85][86][87]

sentences.en: In 1959, Freeman Dyson observed that every developing human civilization constantly increases its energy consumption, and he conjectured that a civilization might try to harness a large part of the energy produced by a star.
sentences.zh: 1959年，弗里曼·戴森观察到，每一个发展中的人类文明都在不断增加其能源消耗，他推测文明可能会尝试利用恒星产生的大部分能量。

blocks.html_en: There have been attempts to find evidence of Dyson spheres that would alter the spectra of their core stars.[88] Direct observation of thousands of galaxies has shown no explicit evidence of artificial construction or modifications.[86][87][89][90] In October 2015, there was speculation that a dimming of light from star KIC 8462852, observed by the Kepler space telescope, could have been a result of such a Dyson sphere under construction.[91][92] However, in 2018, further observations determined that the amount of dimming varied by the frequency of the light, pointing to dust, rather than an opaque object such as a Dyson sphere, as the cause of the dimming.[93][94]

blocks.html_en: Hypothetical explanations for the paradox
[edit]
Rarity of intelligent life
[edit]

Those who think that intelligent extraterrestrial life is (nearly) impossible argue that the conditions needed for the evolution of life—or at least the evolution of biological complexity—are rare or even unique to Earth. Under this assumption, called the rare Earth hypothesis, a rejection of the mediocrity principle, complex multicellular life is regarded as exceedingly unusual.[95]

sentences.en: Those who think that intelligent extraterrestrial life is (nearly) impossible argue that the conditions needed for the evolution of life—or at least the evolution of biological complexity—are rare or even unique to Earth.
sentences.zh: 那些认为外星智慧生命（几乎）不可能存在的人认为，生命进化所需的条件——或者至少是生物复杂性的进化——对于地球来说是罕见的，甚至是独一无二的。

sentences.en: Under this assumption, called the rare Earth hypothesis, a rejection of the mediocrity principle, complex multicellular life is regarded as exceedingly unusual.[95]
sentences.zh: 在这个被称为稀土假说的假设下，对平庸原则的拒绝，复杂的多细胞生命被认为是极其不寻常的。 [95]

blocks.html_en: The rare Earth hypothesis argues that the evolution of biological complexity requires a host of fortuitous circumstances, such as a galactic habitable zone, a star and planet(s) having the requisite conditions, such as enough of a continuous habitable zone, the advantage of a giant guardian like Jupiter and a large moon, conditions needed to ensure the planet has a magnetosphere and plate tectonics,[96] the chemistry of the lithosphere, atmosphere, and oceans, the role of "evolutionary pumps" such as massive glaciation and rare bolide impacts. Perhaps most importantly, advanced life needs whatever it was that led to the transition of (some) prokaryotic cells to eukaryotic cells, sexual reproduction and the Cambrian explosion.

sentences.en: The rare Earth hypothesis argues that the evolution of biological complexity requires a host of fortuitous circumstances, such as a galactic habitable zone, a star and planet(s) having the requisite conditions, such as enough of a continuous habitable zone, the advantage of a giant guardian like Jupiter and a large moon, conditions needed to ensure the planet has a magnetosphere and plate tectonics,[96] the chemistry of the lithosphere, atmosphere, and oceans, the role of "evolutionary pumps" such as massive glaciation and rare bolide impacts.
sentences.zh: 稀土假说认为，生物复杂性的进化需要一系列偶然的环境，例如银河系宜居带、具有必要条件的恒星和行星，例如足够的连续宜居带、像木星和大卫星这样的巨型守护者的优势、确保行星拥有磁层和板块构造所需的条件、[96]岩石圈、大气和海洋的化学成分、“进化泵”的作用等如大规模的冰川作用和罕见的火流星撞击。

sentences.en: Perhaps most importantly, advanced life needs whatever it was that led to the transition of (some) prokaryotic cells to eukaryotic cells, sexual reproduction and the Cambrian explosion.
sentences.zh: 也许最重要的是，高级生命需要任何导致（某些）原核细胞向真核细胞转变、有性繁殖和寒武纪大爆发的东西。

blocks.html_en: In his book Wonderful Life (1989), Stephen Jay Gould suggested that if the "tape of life" were rewound to the time of the Cambrian explosion, and one or two tweaks made, human beings probably never would have evolved. Other thinkers such as Fontana, Buss, and Kauffman have written about the self-organizing properties of life.[97] On the other hand, maybe the filter is further back in time: recently, astrophysicist Matt O'Dowd has identified the eukaryogenesis as a reasonable candidate for such a filter in the past[98] given the increasing difficulties in finding new useful proteins for prokaryotes.[99]

sentences.en: In his book Wonderful Life (1989), Stephen Jay Gould suggested that if the "tape of life" were rewound to the time of the Cambrian explosion, and one or two tweaks made, human beings probably never would have evolved.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德在他的《美好生活》（1989）一书中提出，如果“生命磁带”倒回寒武纪大爆发时期，并进行一两次调整，人类可能永远不会进化。

sentences.en: Other thinkers such as Fontana, Buss, and Kauffman have written about the self-organizing properties of life.[97] On the other hand, maybe the filter is further back in time: recently, astrophysicist Matt O'Dowd has identified the eukaryogenesis as a reasonable candidate for such a filter in the past[98] given the increasing difficulties in finding new useful proteins for prokaryotes.[99]
sentences.zh: 其他思想家，如丰塔纳、巴斯和考夫曼，都写过关于生命自组织特性的文章。 [97]另一方面，也许这个过滤器的时间更早：最近，天体物理学家马特·奥多德（Matt O'Dowd）已经确定真核发生是过去这种过滤器的合理候选者[98]，因为寻找对原核生物有用的新蛋白质越来越困难。 [99]

blocks.html_en: It is possible that even if complex life is common, intelligence (and consequently civilizations) is not.[52] While there are remote sensing techniques that could perhaps detect life-bearing planets without relying on the signs of technology,[100][101] none of them have the ability to determine if any detected life is intelligent. This is sometimes referred to as the "algae vs. alumnae" problem.[102]

sentences.zh: 即使复杂的生命很常见，智能（以及由此产生的文明）也可能不常见。 [52]虽然有些遥感技术或许可以在不依赖技术迹象的情况下探测到存在生命的行星，[100][101]但它们都没有能力确定任何探测到的生命是否具有智慧。

sentences.en: This is sometimes referred to as the "algae vs. alumnae" problem.[102]
sentences.zh: 这有时被称为“藻类与校友”问题。 [102]

blocks.html_en: Charles Lineweaver states that when considering any extreme trait in an animal, intermediate stages do not necessarily produce "inevitable" outcomes. For example, large brains are no more "inevitable", or convergent, than are the long noses of animals such as aardvarks and elephants. As he points out, "dolphins have had ~20 million years to build a radio telescope and have not done so".[52] In addition, Rebecca Boyle points out that of all the species that have evolved in the history of life on the planet Earth, only one—human beings and only in the beginning stages—has ever become space-faring.[103]

sentences.en: Charles Lineweaver states that when considering any extreme trait in an animal, intermediate stages do not necessarily produce "inevitable" outcomes.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·莱恩韦弗 (Charles Lineweaver) 指出，在考虑动物的任何极端特征时，中间阶段不一定会产生“不可避免”的结果。

sentences.en: For example, large brains are no more "inevitable", or convergent, than are the long noses of animals such as aardvarks and elephants.
sentences.zh: 例如，大大脑并不比土豚和大象等动物的长鼻子更“不可避免”或趋同。

sentences.en: As he points out, "dolphins have had ~20 million years to build a radio telescope and have not done so".[52] In addition, Rebecca Boyle points out that of all the species that have evolved in the history of life on the planet Earth, only one—human beings and only in the beginning stages—has ever become space-faring.[103]
sentences.zh: 正如他指出的，“海豚花了大约 2000 万年的时间建造射电望远镜，但还没有这样做”。 [52]此外，丽贝卡·博伊尔指出，在地球生命史上进化的所有物种中，只有一个——人类，而且还只是处于起步阶段——曾经进入太空。 [103]

blocks.html_en: Given that the expected lifespan of the universe is at least one trillion years and the age of the universe is around 14 billion years, it is possible that humans have emerged at or near the earliest possible opportunity for intelligent life to evolve. Avi Loeb, an astrophysicist and cosmologist, has suggested that Earth may be a very early example of a life-bearing planet and that life-bearing planets may be more likely trillions of years from now. He has put forward the view that the Universe has only recently reached a state in which life is possible and this is the reason humanity has not detected extraterrestrial life. The firstborn hypothesis posits that humans are the first, or one of the first, intelligent species to evolve. Therefore, many intelligent species may eventually exist, but few, if any, currently do. Moreover, it is possible that said species, even if they already exist, are developing more slowly, or have more limited resources on their home world, meaning that they may take longer than humans have to achieve spaceflight.

sentences.en: Given that the expected lifespan of the universe is at least one trillion years and the age of the universe is around 14 billion years, it is possible that humans have emerged at or near the earliest possible opportunity for intelligent life to evolve.
sentences.zh: 鉴于宇宙的预期寿命至少为一万亿年，而宇宙的年龄约为140亿年，人类有可能在智慧生命进化的最早时机出现或接近出现。

sentences.zh: 他提出了这样的观点：宇宙最近才达到了可能存在生命的状态，这就是人类尚未发现外星生命的原因。

sentences.zh: 长子假说认为，人类是第一个或第一个进化出的智慧物种。

sentences.en: Therefore, many intelligent species may eventually exist, but few, if any, currently do.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多智慧物种最终可能会存在，但目前存在的却很少。

sentences.en: Moreover, it is possible that said species, even if they already exist, are developing more slowly, or have more limited resources on their home world, meaning that they may take longer than humans have to achieve spaceflight.

blocks.html_en: Periodic extinction by natural events

sentences.zh: 自然事件导致的周期性灭绝

blocks.html_en: [edit]

sentences.en: An asteroid impact may trigger an extinction event.
sentences.zh: 小行星撞击可能引发灭绝事件。

blocks.html_en: New life might commonly die out due to runaway heating or cooling on their fledgling planets.[104] On Earth, there have been numerous major extinction events that destroyed the majority of complex species alive at the time; the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs is the best known example. These are thought to have been caused by events such as impact from a large asteroid, massive volcanic eruptions, or astronomical events such as gamma-ray bursts.[105] It may be the case that such extinction events are common throughout the universe and periodically destroy intelligent life, or at least its civilizations, before the species is able to develop the technology to communicate with other intelligent species.[106]

sentences.en: New life might commonly die out due to runaway heating or cooling on their fledgling planets.[104] On Earth, there have been numerous major extinction events that destroyed the majority of complex species alive at the time; the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs is the best known example.
sentences.zh: 新生命通常可能会因新生行星失控的加热或冷却而灭绝。[104]在地球上，发生过许多重大的灭绝事件，摧毁了当时活着的大多数复杂物种。非鸟类恐龙的灭绝是最著名的例子。

sentences.en: These are thought to have been caused by events such as impact from a large asteroid, massive volcanic eruptions, or astronomical events such as gamma-ray bursts.[105] It may be the case that such extinction events are common throughout the universe and periodically destroy intelligent life, or at least its civilizations, before the species is able to develop the technology to communicate with other intelligent species.[106]
sentences.zh: 这些被认为是由大型小行星撞击、大规模火山喷发或伽马射线爆发等天文事件等事件引起的。 [105]情况可能是这样的灭绝事件在整个宇宙中很常见，并在该物种能够开发出与其他智能物种交流的技术之前周期性地摧毁智能生命，或者至少是它的文明。 [106]

blocks.html_en: However, the chances of extinction by natural events may be very low on the scale of a civilization's lifetime. Based on an analysis of impact craters on Earth and the Moon, the average interval between impacts large enough to cause global consequences (like the Chicxulub impact) is estimated to be around 100 million years.[107]

sentences.en: However, the chances of extinction by natural events may be very low on the scale of a civilization's lifetime.
sentences.zh: 然而，就文明的一生而言，因自然事件而灭绝的可能性可能非常低。

sentences.en: Based on an analysis of impact craters on Earth and the Moon, the average interval between impacts large enough to cause global consequences (like the Chicxulub impact) is estimated to be around 100 million years.[107]
sentences.zh: 根据对地球和月球撞击坑的分析，足以造成全球后果（如希克苏鲁伯撞击）的撞击之间的平均间隔估计约为 1 亿年。 [107]

blocks.html_en: Evolutionary explanations
[edit]
It is the nature of intelligent life to destroy itself

sentences.en: It is the nature of intelligent life to destroy itself
sentences.zh: 自我毁灭是智慧生命的本质

blocks.html_en: [edit]

sentences.en: A 23-kiloton tower shot called BADGER, fired as part of the Operation Upshot–Knothole nuclear test series
sentences.zh: 一枚名为 BADGER 的 23 吨塔式炮弹，作为“结果行动 - 诺霍尔”核试验系列的一部分发射

blocks.html_en: This is the argument that technological civilizations may usually or invariably destroy themselves before or shortly after developing radio or spaceflight technology. The astrophysicist Sebastian von Hoerner stated that the progress of science and technology on Earth was driven by two factors—the struggle for domination and the desire for an easy life. The former potentially leads to complete destruction, while the latter may lead to biological or mental degeneration.[108] Possible means of annihilation via major global issues, where global interconnectedness actually makes humanity more vulnerable than resilient,[109] are many,[4] including war, accidental environmental contamination or damage, the development of biotechnology,[110] synthetic life like mirror life,[111] resource depletion, climate change,[112] or artificial intelligence. This general theme is explored both in fiction and in scientific hypotheses.[113]

sentences.en: This is the argument that technological civilizations may usually or invariably destroy themselves before or shortly after developing radio or spaceflight technology.
sentences.zh: 这种论点认为，技术文明通常或总是在发展无线电或航天技术之前或之后不久就会毁灭自己。

sentences.en: The astrophysicist Sebastian von Hoerner stated that the progress of science and technology on Earth was driven by two factors—the struggle for domination and the desire for an easy life.
sentences.zh: 天体物理学家塞巴斯蒂安·冯·霍尔纳表示，地球科学技术的进步是由两个因素驱动的：争夺统治地位的斗争和对安逸生活的渴望。

sentences.en: The former potentially leads to complete destruction, while the latter may lead to biological or mental degeneration.[108] Possible means of annihilation via major global issues, where global interconnectedness actually makes humanity more vulnerable than resilient,[109] are many,[4] including war, accidental environmental contamination or damage, the development of biotechnology,[110] synthetic life like mirror life,[111] resource depletion, climate change,[112] or artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 前者可能导致彻底破坏，而后者可能导致生物或精神退化。 [108]通过重大全球问题进行毁灭的可能手段是，全球互联性实际上使人类更加脆弱，而不是坚韧，[109] 有很多，[4] 包括战争、意外环境污染或破坏、生物技术的发展、[110] 镜像生命等合成生命、[111] 资源枯竭、气候变化、[112] 或人工智能。

sentences.en: This general theme is explored both in fiction and in scientific hypotheses.[113]
sentences.zh: 这个一般主题在小说和科学假设中都有探讨。[113]

blocks.html_en: In 1966, Sagan and Shklovskii speculated that technological civilizations will either tend to destroy themselves within a century of developing interstellar communicative capability or master their self-destructive tendencies and survive for billion-year timescales.[114] Self-annihilation may also be viewed in terms of thermodynamics: insofar as life is an ordered system that can sustain itself against the tendency to disorder, Stephen Hawking's "external transmission" or interstellar communicative phase, where knowledge production and knowledge management is more important than transmission of information via evolution, may be the point at which the system becomes unstable and self-destructs.[115][116] Here, Hawking emphasizes self-design of the human genome (transhumanism) or enhancement via machines (e.g., brain–computer interface) to enhance human intelligence and reduce aggression, without which he implies human civilization may be too stupid collectively to survive an increasingly unstable system. For instance, the development of technologies during the "external transmission" phase, such as weaponization of artificial general intelligence or antimatter, may not be met by concomitant increases in human ability to manage its own inventions. Consequently, disorder increases in the system: global governance may become increasingly destabilized, worsening humanity's ability to manage the possible means of annihilation listed above, resulting in global societal collapse.

sentences.en: In 1966, Sagan and Shklovskii speculated that technological civilizations will either tend to destroy themselves within a century of developing interstellar communicative capability or master their self-destructive tendencies and survive for billion-year timescales.[114] Self-annihilation may also be viewed in terms of thermodynamics: insofar as life is an ordered system that can sustain itself against the tendency to disorder, Stephen Hawking's "external transmission" or interstellar communicative phase, where knowledge production and knowledge management is more important than transmission of information via evolution, may be the point at which the system becomes unstable and self-destructs.[115][116] Here, Hawking emphasizes self-design of the human genome (transhumanism) or enhancement via machines (e.g., brain–computer interface) to enhance human intelligence and reduce aggression, without which he implies human civilization may be too stupid collectively to survive an increasingly unstable system.
sentences.zh: 1966年，萨根和什克洛夫斯基推测，技术文明要么会在星际通信能力发展的一个世纪内趋于自我毁灭，要么掌握其自我毁灭的倾向并在数十亿年的时间尺度内生存。 [114]自我毁灭也可以从热力学的角度来看待：只要生命是一个有序的系统，可以维持自身免受无序倾向的影响，斯蒂芬·霍金的“外部传输”或星际交流阶段，其中知识生产和知识管理比通过进化传递信息更重要，可能是系统变得不稳定和自我毁灭的点。 [115][116]在这里，霍金强调人类基因组的自我设计（超人类主义）或通过机器（例如脑机接口）进行增强，以增强人类智力并减少攻击性，否则他暗示人类文明可能会集体过于愚蠢，无法在日益不稳定的系统中生存。

sentences.en: For instance, the development of technologies during the "external transmission" phase, such as weaponization of artificial general intelligence or antimatter, may not be met by concomitant increases in human ability to manage its own inventions.
sentences.zh: 例如，“外部传输”阶段的技术发展，例如通用人工智能或反物质的武器化，可能无法通过人类管理自己发明的能力的随之提高来满足。

sentences.en: Consequently, disorder increases in the system: global governance may become increasingly destabilized, worsening humanity's ability to manage the possible means of annihilation listed above, resulting in global societal collapse.
sentences.zh: 结果，系统中的无序性增加：全球治理可能变得越来越不稳定，削弱人类管理上述可能的毁灭手段的能力，导致全球社会崩溃。

blocks.html_en: A less theoretical example might be the resource-depletion issue on Polynesian islands, of which Easter Island is only the best known. David Brin points out that during the expansion phase from 1500 BC to 800 AD there were cycles of overpopulation followed by what might be called periodic cullings of adult males through war or ritual. He writes, "There are many stories of islands whose men were almost wiped out—sometimes by internal strife, and sometimes by invading males from other islands."[117]

sentences.en: A less theoretical example might be the resource-depletion issue on Polynesian islands, of which Easter Island is only the best known.
sentences.zh: 一个不太理论化的例子可能是波利尼西亚群岛的资源枯竭问题，其中复活节岛是最著名的。

sentences.en: David Brin points out that during the expansion phase from 1500 BC to 800 AD there were cycles of overpopulation followed by what might be called periodic cullings of adult males through war or ritual.
sentences.zh: 大卫·布林 (David Brin) 指出，在公元前 1500 年至公元 800 年的扩张阶段，出现了人口过剩的循环，随后通过战争或仪式周期性地宰杀成年男性。

sentences.en: He writes, "There are many stories of islands whose men were almost wiped out—sometimes by internal strife, and sometimes by invading males from other islands."[117]
sentences.zh: 他写道，“有很多关于岛屿上的人类几乎被消灭的故事——有时是由于内部冲突，有时是由于来自其他岛屿的男性入侵。”[117]

blocks.html_en: Using extinct civilizations such as Easter Island as models, a study conducted in 2018 by Adam Frank et al. posited that climate change induced by "energy intensive" civilizations may prevent sustainability within such civilizations, thus explaining the paradoxical lack of evidence for intelligent extraterrestrial life. Based on dynamical systems theory, the study examined how technological civilizations (exo-civilizations) consume resources and the feedback effects this consumption has on their planets and its carrying capacity. According to Adam Frank "[t]he point is to recognize that driving climate change may be something generic. The laws of physics demand that any young population, building an energy-intensive civilization like ours, is going to have feedback on its planet. Seeing climate change in this cosmic context may give us better insight into what's happening to us now and how to deal with it."[118] Generalizing the Anthropocene, their model produces four different outcomes:

sentences.en: Using extinct civilizations such as Easter Island as models, a study conducted in 2018 by Adam Frank et al. posited that climate change induced by "energy intensive" civilizations may prevent sustainability within such civilizations, thus explaining the paradoxical lack of evidence for intelligent extraterrestrial life.
sentences.zh: Adam Frank 等人于 2018 年进行的一项研究以复活节岛等灭绝的文明为模型。假设“能源密集型”文明引起的气候变化可能会阻碍此类文明的可持续性，从而解释了为何缺乏存在智慧外星生命的证据。

sentences.zh: 该研究基于动力系统理论，考察了技术文明（外文明）如何消耗资源以及这种消耗对其行星及其承载能力的反馈影响。

sentences.en: According to Adam Frank "[t]he point is to recognize that driving climate change may be something generic.
sentences.zh: 亚当·弗兰克 (Adam Frank) 表示，“重点是要认识到推动气候变化可能是一种普遍现象。

sentences.en: The laws of physics demand that any young population, building an energy-intensive civilization like ours, is going to have feedback on its planet.
sentences.zh: 物理定律要求任何建立像我们这样的能源密集型文明的年轻人都将在其星球上得到反馈。

sentences.en: Seeing climate change in this cosmic context may give us better insight into what's happening to us now and how to deal with it."[118] Generalizing the Anthropocene, their model produces four different outcomes:
sentences.zh: 在这个宇宙背景下看待气候变化可能会让我们更好地了解现在发生在我们身上的事情以及如何应对它。”[118]概括人类世，他们的模型产生了四种不同的结果：

sentences.en: Possible trajectories of anthropogenic climate change in a model by Frank et al., 2018
sentences.zh: Frank 等人 2018 年模型中人为气候变化的可能轨迹

blocks.html_en: • Die-off: A scenario where the population grows quickly, surpassing the planet's carrying capacity, which leads to a peak followed by a rapid decline. The population eventually stabilizes at a much lower equilibrium level, allowing the planet to partially recover.

sentences.en: Die-off: A scenario where the population grows quickly, surpassing the planet's carrying capacity, which leads to a peak followed by a rapid decline.
sentences.zh: 死亡：人口快速增长，超过地球的承载能力，导致达到顶峰，然后迅速下降的情况。

sentences.en: The population eventually stabilizes at a much lower equilibrium level, allowing the planet to partially recover.
sentences.zh: 人口最终稳定在一个低得多的平衡水平，使地球得以部分恢复。

blocks.html_en: • Sustainability: A scenario where civilizations successfully transition from high-impact resources (like fossil fuels) to sustainable ones (like solar energy) before significant environmental degradation occurs. This allows the civilization and planet to reach a stable equilibrium, avoiding catastrophic effects.

sentences.en: Sustainability: A scenario where civilizations successfully transition from high-impact resources (like fossil fuels) to sustainable ones (like solar energy) before significant environmental degradation occurs.
sentences.zh: 可持续性：在环境严重退化发生之前，文明成功地从高影响资源（如化石燃料）过渡到可持续资源（如太阳能）的场景。

sentences.en: This allows the civilization and planet to reach a stable equilibrium, avoiding catastrophic effects.
sentences.zh: 这使得文明和星球能够达到稳定的平衡，避免灾难性的影响。

blocks.html_en: • Collapse Without Resource Change: In this trajectory, the population and environmental degradation increase rapidly. The civilization does not switch to sustainable resources in time, leading to a total collapse where a tipping point is crossed and the population drops.

sentences.en: Collapse Without Resource Change: In this trajectory, the population and environmental degradation increase rapidly.
sentences.zh: 资源不变化就会崩溃：在这个轨迹中，人口和环境退化迅速增加。

sentences.en: The civilization does not switch to sustainable resources in time, leading to a total collapse where a tipping point is crossed and the population drops.
sentences.zh: 文明没有及时转向可持续资源，导致全面崩溃，跨越临界点，人口下降。

blocks.html_en: • Collapse With Resource Change: Similar to the previous scenario, but in this case, the civilization attempts to transition to sustainable resources. However, the change comes too late, and the environmental damage is irreversible, still leading to the civilization's collapse.[119][120]

sentences.en: Collapse With Resource Change: Similar to the previous scenario, but in this case, the civilization attempts to transition to sustainable resources.
sentences.zh: 资源变化导致崩溃：与之前的场景类似，但在这种情况下，文明试图过渡到可持续资源。

sentences.en: However, the change comes too late, and the environmental damage is irreversible, still leading to the civilization's collapse.[119][120]
sentences.zh: 然而，改变来得太晚了，环境破坏是不可逆转的，仍然导致文明的崩溃。[119][120]

blocks.html_en: Only one intelligent species can exist in a given region of space

sentences.en: Only one intelligent species can exist in a given region of space
sentences.zh: 在给定的空间区域中只能存在一种智慧物种

blocks.html_en: [edit]

Another hypothesis is that an intelligent species beyond a certain point of technological capability will destroy other intelligent species as they appear, perhaps by using self-replicating probes. Science fiction writer Fred Saberhagen has explored this idea in his Berserker series, as has physicist Gregory Benford[121] and also, science fiction writer Greg Bear in his The Forge of God novel,[122] and later Liu Cixin in his The Three-Body Problem series.

sentences.en: Another hypothesis is that an intelligent species beyond a certain point of technological capability will destroy other intelligent species as they appear, perhaps by using self-replicating probes.
sentences.zh: 另一个假设是，超出一定技术能力的智能物种可能会通过使用自我复制探针来摧毁其他出现的智能物种。

sentences.en: Science fiction writer Fred Saberhagen has explored this idea in his Berserker series, as has physicist Gregory Benford[121] and also, science fiction writer Greg Bear in his The Forge of God novel,[122] and later Liu Cixin in his The Three-Body Problem series.
sentences.zh: 科幻小说作家 Fred Saberhagen 在他的《狂战士》系列中探索了这个想法，物理学家格雷戈里·本福德[121]、科幻小说作家格雷格·贝尔在他的《上帝熔炉》小说中也探索过这个想法，[122] 以及后来的刘慈欣在他的《三体》系列中也探索过这个想法。

blocks.html_en: A species might undertake such extermination out of expansionist motives, greed, paranoia, or aggression. In 1981, cosmologist Edward Harrison argued that such behavior would be an act of prudence: an intelligent species that has overcome its own self-destructive tendencies might view any other species bent on galactic expansion as a threat.[123] It has also been suggested that a successful alien species would be a superpredator, as are humans.[124][125] Another possibility invokes the "tragedy of the commons" and the anthropic principle: the first lifeform to achieve interstellar travel will necessarily (even if unintentionally) prevent competitors from arising, and humans simply happen to be first.[126][127]

sentences.en: A species might undertake such extermination out of expansionist motives, greed, paranoia, or aggression.
sentences.zh: 一个物种可能出于扩张主义动机、贪婪、偏执或侵略而进行这种灭绝。

sentences.en: In 1981, cosmologist Edward Harrison argued that such behavior would be an act of prudence: an intelligent species that has overcome its own self-destructive tendencies might view any other species bent on galactic expansion as a threat.[123] It has also been suggested that a successful alien species would be a superpredator, as are humans.[124][125] Another possibility invokes the "tragedy of the commons" and the anthropic principle: the first lifeform to achieve interstellar travel will necessarily (even if unintentionally) prevent competitors from arising, and humans simply happen to be first.[126][127]
sentences.zh: 1981 年，宇宙学家爱德华·哈里森 (Edward Harrison) 认为，这种行为是一种谨慎的行为：一个克服了自我毁灭倾向的智慧物种可能会将任何其他致力于银河扩张的物种视为威胁。 [123]还有人认为，成功的外来物种将是超级掠食者，就像人类一样。 [124][125]另一种可能性援引了“公地悲剧”和人择原理：第一个实现星际旅行的生命形式必然（即使是无意的）阻止竞争对手的出现，而人类恰好是第一个。 [126][127]

blocks.html_en: Civilizations only broadcast detectable signals for a brief period of time

sentences.en: Civilizations only broadcast detectable signals for a brief period of time
sentences.zh: 文明仅在短时间内广播可检测到的信号

blocks.html_en: [edit]

It may be that alien civilizations are detectable through their radio emissions for only a short time, reducing the likelihood of spotting them. The usual assumption is that civilizations outgrow radio through technological advancement.[128] However, there could be other leakage such as that from microwaves used to transmit power from solar satellites to ground receivers.[129] Regarding the first point, in a 2006 Sky & Telescope article, Seth Shostak wrote, "Moreover, radio leakage from a planet is only likely to get weaker as a civilization advances and its communications technology gets better. Earth itself is increasingly switching from broadcasts to leakage-free cables and fiber optics, and from primitive but obvious carrier-wave broadcasts to subtler, hard-to-recognize spread-spectrum transmissions."[130]

sentences.en: It may be that alien civilizations are detectable through their radio emissions for only a short time, reducing the likelihood of spotting them.
sentences.zh: 外星文明可能只能在很短的时间内通过其无线电发射被探测到，从而降低了发现它们的可能性。

sentences.en: The usual assumption is that civilizations outgrow radio through technological advancement.[128] However, there could be other leakage such as that from microwaves used to transmit power from solar satellites to ground receivers.[129] Regarding the first point, in a 2006 Sky & Telescope article, Seth Shostak wrote, "Moreover, radio leakage from a planet is only likely to get weaker as a civilization advances and its communications technology gets better.
sentences.zh: 通常的假设是，文明通过技术进步而超越了无线电。[128]然而，可能存在其他泄漏，例如用于从太阳能卫星向地面接收器传输电力的微波的泄漏。[129]关于第一点，Seth Shostak在2006年《天空与望远镜》的一篇文章中写道：“此外，随着文明的进步和通信技术的进步，来自行星的无线电泄漏只会变得更弱。

sentences.en: Earth itself is increasingly switching from broadcasts to leakage-free cables and fiber optics, and from primitive but obvious carrier-wave broadcasts to subtler, hard-to-recognize spread-spectrum transmissions."[130]
sentences.zh: 地球本身正在逐渐从广播转向无泄漏电缆和光纤，从原始但明显的载波广播转向更微妙、难以识别的扩频传输。”[130]

blocks.html_en: More hypothetically, advanced alien civilizations may evolve beyond broadcasting at all in the electromagnetic spectrum and communicate by technologies not developed or used by mankind.[131] Some scientists have hypothesized that advanced civilizations may send neutrino signals.[132] If such signals exist, they could be detectable by neutrino detectors that are as of 2009 under construction for other goals.[133]

sentences.en: More hypothetically, advanced alien civilizations may evolve beyond broadcasting at all in the electromagnetic spectrum and communicate by technologies not developed or used by mankind.[131] Some scientists have hypothesized that advanced civilizations may send neutrino signals.[132] If such signals exist, they could be detectable by neutrino detectors that are as of 2009 under construction for other goals.[133]
sentences.zh: 更假设的是，先进的外星文明可能在电磁频谱中完全超越广播，并通过人类未开发或使用的技术进行通信。 [131]一些科学家假设先进文明可能会发送中微子信号。 [132]如果存在这样的信号，它们可以被中微子探测器探测到，截至 2009 年，中微子探测器正在为其他目标而建造。 [133]

Aliens may be psychologically unwilling to attempt to communicate with human beings. Perhaps human mathematics is parochial to Earth and not shared by other life,[134] though others argue this can only apply to abstract math since the math associated with physics must be similar (in results, if not in methods).[135]

sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是，人类理论家低估了外星生命与地球生命的差异。

sentences.en: Aliens may be psychologically unwilling to attempt to communicate with human beings.
sentences.zh: 外星人可能在心理上不愿意尝试与人类交流。

sentences.en: Perhaps human mathematics is parochial to Earth and not shared by other life,[134] though others argue this can only apply to abstract math since the math associated with physics must be similar (in results, if not in methods).[135]

blocks.html_en: In his 2009 book, SETI scientist Seth Shostak wrote, "Our experiments [such as plans to use drilling rigs on Mars] are still looking for the type of extraterrestrial that would have appealed to Percival Lowell [astronomer who believed he had observed canals on Mars]."[136]

sentences.zh: SETI 科学家塞思·肖斯塔克 (Seth Shostak) 在其 2009 年的书中写道，“我们的实验（例如在火星上使用钻机的计划）仍在寻找能够吸引珀西瓦尔·洛厄尔（Percival Lowell）（相信他在火星上观察到运河的天文学家）的外星人类型。”[136]

blocks.html_en: Physiology might also be a communication barrier. Carl Sagan speculated that an alien species might have a thought process orders of magnitude slower (or faster) than that of humans.[137] A message broadcast by that species might seem like random background noise to humans, and therefore go undetected.

blocks.html_en: Paul Davies stated that 500 years ago the very idea of a computer doing work merely by manipulating internal data may not have been viewed as a technology at all. There is no vocabulary to describe the third level, but that doesn't mean it is non-existent, and we need to be open to the possibility that alien technology may operate at the third level, or maybe the fourth, fifth [...] levels."[138]

Clarke hypothesized that "our technology must still be laughably primitive; we may well be like jungle savages listening for the throbbing of tom-toms, while the ether around them carries more words per second than they could utter in a lifetime".[139] Another thought is that technological civilizations invariably experience a technological singularity and attain a post-biological character.[140]

blocks.html_en: Sociological explanations
[edit]
Expansionism is not the cosmic norm

sentences.en: Expansionism is not the cosmic norm
sentences.zh: 扩张主义不是宇宙常态

blocks.html_en: [edit]

In response to Tipler's idea of self-replicating probes, Stephen Jay Gould wrote, "I must confess that I simply don't know how to react to such arguments. I have enough trouble predicting the plans and reactions of the people closest to me. I am usually baffled by the thoughts and accomplishments of humans in different cultures. I'll be damned if I can state with certainty what some extraterrestrial source of intelligence might do."[141][142]

sentences.en: In response to Tipler's idea of self-replicating probes, Stephen Jay Gould wrote, "I must confess that I simply don't know how to react to such arguments.

sentences.en: I have enough trouble predicting the plans and reactions of the people closest to me.
sentences.zh: 我很难预测最亲近的人的计划和反应。
